items.originalTitle: F1公布2027赛季赛历：24站比赛，10个冲刺赛周末
items.summaryEn: F1 has unveiled its 24-race calendar for the 2027 season, increasing the number of sprint weekends to 10, with Monaco hosting a sprint race for the first time. The season starts in Bahrain on 14 March and finishes in Abu Dhabi.
detailZh: F1 公布2027年赛历——摩纳哥成为10场冲刺赛之一
摩纳哥将在2027年首次承办F1冲刺赛，同时锦标赛在新公布的24场比赛赛历中，把冲刺赛的数量从6场扩大到10场
F1 公布了2027赛季的24场比赛赛历，将冲刺赛周末的数量增加到10场。新赛季将在巴林揭幕，并在阿布扎比收官。
2027赛季定于3月14日以巴林大奖赛拉开帷幕，该项赛事回归其惯常的揭幕战位置，并与沙特阿拉伯组成背靠背双连赛，而墨尔本的澳大利亚大奖赛则成为赛历上的第三场比赛。
在日本站和中国站之后，F1 将于五月前往迈阿密和蒙特利尔。这两场比赛仍相隔三周，但加拿大赛定在 5 月 23 日，意味着这场比赛不会与印地车赛（IndyCar）的印第安纳波利斯 500 大赛冲突。
F1 将于 6 月 6 日的摩纳哥大奖赛首次重返欧洲。有趣的是，这条狭窄的街道赛道本来无法进行任何超车，却将首次举办冲刺赛（sprint 比赛）。据了解，F1 希望借助摩纳哥排位赛的观赏性，在周五和周六安排两场独立的排位赛。
葡萄牙自 2021 年以来首次重返赛历，将于 6 月 20 日在波尔蒂芒的阿尔加维赛道举行比赛。英国大奖赛紧随其后，于 7 月 4 日在银石赛道举行，随后是奥地利、比利时和匈牙利站，其中匈牙利站于 8 月 1 日为赛季上半程画上句号。
巴林计划承办赛前测试以及 2027 赛季的揭幕战
夏休期结束后，比赛将于9月5日继续在意大利进行，随后是马德里。与葡萄牙一样，土耳其也将于10月3日重返赛历，作为巴库和新加坡之间三连赛中的中间一站。
接下来在美洲还有另一个三连赛，包括奥斯汀、墨西哥和巴西，而拉斯维加斯大奖赛则于11月20日成为一场独立的分站赛。
赛季预计将以卡塔尔和阿布扎比的背靠背双连赛收官，两站都将采用冲刺赛赛制。
摩纳哥是组织冲刺赛的十个分站之一
摩纳哥是赛历上10场冲刺赛之一，比之前的6场有所增加，一级方程式管理层出于商业原因希望扩大其数量。巴林、澳大利亚、日本和阿布扎比也将迎来冲刺赛首秀，同时该赛制将回归加拿大、英国、意大利、巴西和卡塔尔。
一级方程式在一份声明中表示：“由于冲刺赛赛制持续取得成功且需求强劲，2027年冲刺赛的数量已从6场增加到10场，为车迷、推广商、转播商和合作伙伴在整个赛季中带来更多精彩的竞技内容。”
“自冲刺赛于2021年推出以来，数据显示，冲刺赛周末的总观看量比非冲刺赛周末高出12%，冲刺赛排位赛对车迷的吸引力最高可达自由练习赛的三倍，82%的冲刺赛周末现场观众表示这为他们的门票增添了价值，75%的一级方程式车迷认为冲刺赛为赛季赛历增添了更大价值。”
葡萄牙将于2027年重返一级方程式赛历
季前测试恢复为在巴林进行的为期四天的单一测试，时间为2月24日至27日。
至于2026赛季的收官安排，F1坚决表示卡塔尔和阿布扎比的比赛将按计划进行，直至另行通知。不过，据Motorsport.com了解，伊莫拉方面正在做准备，以便在阿布扎比的那个周末承办赛季收官战，因为考虑到该地区持续的冲突，很可能出现中东两站比赛都无法举办的情况。
F2已经在巴库的赛程中增加了一场额外的比赛，这表明这项方程式系列赛正打算加强其赛季末段的安排。
“2027年的赛历汇集了世界上一些最具标志性的赛道和最具活力的城市，为又一个令人难忘的F1赛季打造了一个绝佳的舞台，”F1首席执行官兼总裁斯特凡诺·多梅尼卡利说，“我们非常高兴地欢迎葡萄牙和土耳其加入锦标赛，并将冲刺赛扩展到十场赛事，为我们的车迷带来更强烈的观赏性、更富戏剧性的场面，以及让这项运动如此特别的贴身缠斗。”
“2027年国际汽联一级方程式世界锦标赛赛程有力地体现了我们这项运动在全球的吸引力和持续增长，”国际汽联主席穆罕默德·本·苏拉耶姆补充道。“赛历横跨五大洲，共设二十四场大奖赛，葡萄牙和土耳其重返赛历，同时还提供了扩大冲刺赛（Sprint）计划的机会，这份赛历将传统、创新与车迷参与相结合，同时保持了最高的体育标准。”
detailEn: F1 announces 2027 calendar - with Monaco among 10 sprint races
Monaco will host an F1 sprint race for the first time in 2027 as the championship expands the format from six to 10 events on its new 24-race calendar
F1 has unveiled its 24-race calendar for the 2027 season, increasing the number of sprint weekends to 10, as it kicks off the season in Bahrain and finishes in Abu Dhabi.

The 2027 season is slated to get underway on 14 March with the Bahrain Grand Prix, which returns to its usual opener slot as a double-header with Saudi Arabia, while Melbourne's Australian Grand Prix becomes the third event on the calendar.
Following events in Japan and China, F1 heads to Miami and Montreal in May. The two events remain three weeks apart, but Canada's 23 May date means the race won't clash with IndyCar's Indy 500.

F1 first heads to Europe with the Monaco Grand Prix on 6 June, which will intriguingly receive a sprint race for the first time despite its tight street circuit not allowing any overtaking. It's understood F1 is keen to lean into Monaco's qualifying spectacle by offering two separate qualifying sessions on Friday and Saturday.

Portugal returns to the calendar for the first time since 2021 with a race at the Algarve circuit in Portimao, taking place on 20 June. The British Grand Prix follows on 4 July at Silverstone, followed by rounds in Austria, Belgium and Hungary, the latter bookending the first half of the season on 1 August.
Bahrain is scheduled to host both pre-season testing and the 2027 season opener

After the summer break, action continues in Italy on 5 September, followed by Madrid. Alongside Portugal, Turkey also returns to the calendar on 3 October, as the middle leg of a triple-header with Baku and Singapore.
Another triple-header follows in the Americas with Austin, Mexico and Brazil, while the Las Vegas Grand Prix becomes a standalone race on 20 November.
The season is scheduled to close with a double-header in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, both featuring a sprint format.
Monaco one of 10 rounds to organise a sprint race

Monaco is one of 10 sprint races on the calendar, up from six, as F1 management was keen to expand its number for commercial reasons. Bahrain, Australia, Japan, and Abu Dhabi are also set for a sprint debut, while the format returns to Canada, Britain, Italy, Brazil and Qatar.

"Due to the continued success and strong demand for the format, the number of Sprint events has increased from six to ten for 2027, delivering even more competitive action across the season for fans, promoters, broadcasters, and partners," F1 said in a statement.

"Since the Sprint was introduced in 2021, the data shows that total viewership of Sprint weekends is 12% higher than non-Sprint weekends, Sprint Qualifying is up to three times more popular with fans than Free Practice, 82% of attendees at Sprint weekends say it adds value to their ticket, and 75% of F1 fans believe Sprint events add greater value to a season’s calendar."
Portugal will return to the F1 calendar in 2027
Pre-season testing reverts to a single four-day test in Bahrain from 24-27 February.

As for the conclusion of the 2026 season, F1 is adamant Qatar and Abu Dhabi will go ahead as scheduled until further notice. However, Motorsport.com understands preparations are ongoing in Imola to host the season finale on the Abu Dhabi weekend in the likely scenario that neither Middle Eastern race can take place given the ongoing conflict in the region.
F2 has already added an additional race to its Baku schedule, an indication that the single-seater series is aiming to bolster the end of its season.

“The 2027 calendar brings together some of the most iconic circuits and vibrant cities in the world, creating an incredible stage for another unforgettable season of Formula 1," said F1 CEO and president Stefano Domenicali. "We are thrilled to welcome Portugal and Türkiye to the championship and to expand Sprint racing to ten events, giving our fans even more intensity, drama, and the wheel-to-wheel action that make our sport so special."

“The 2027 FIA Formula One World Championship calendar is a strong reflection of the global appeal and continued growth of our sport," FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem added. "With twenty-four Grands Prix across five continents, the return of Portugal and Türkiye, and the opportunity for an expanded Sprint programme, the calendar combines tradition, innovation, and fan engagement while maintaining the highest sporting standards."

detailZh: 塞巴斯蒂安·维特尔：“我会非常高兴”基米·安东内利打破我F1最年轻冠军的纪录
随着安东内利逐渐接近首个世界冠军，维特尔预计自己的纪录将被打破——并且对此感到高兴
塞巴斯蒂安·维特尔表示，如果基米·安东内利打破他保持的F1最年轻世界冠军纪录，他会“非常高兴”。
维特尔于2010年以23岁4个月11天的年龄夺得该头衔，比刘易斯·汉密尔顿2008年的纪录提前了五个半月。
安东内利如今越来越有可能在年仅20岁时赢得今年的年度冠军，他在西班牙大奖赛的胜利将领先主要挑战者、梅赛德斯队友乔治·拉塞尔的优势扩大到81分。
“我会为他感到非常高兴，”维特尔在蒙扎说。“他度过了不可思议的一年。有句老话说，纪录就是用来打破的。他还有很多年可以去做到这一点。
“我热爱这项运动，所以作为观众非常兴奋。我希望其他人能回来，更多地参与竞争。我是独立的，为他感到高兴，因为我知道背后有多少努力才能实现，无论谁赢都当之无愧。”
塞巴斯蒂安·维特尔在阿布扎比赢得2010年世界冠军
安东内利已经打破了维特尔的一些纪录。这位意大利年轻车手今年19岁时获得了首个杆位和首个帽子戏法，而德国人在2008年和2009年21岁时才实现这些成就。
这位梅赛德斯车手对前辈的鼓励表示感谢：“太棒了。塞布不可思议。他是我的朋友，每个比赛周末后甚至有些比赛前都会发消息。
“看到他的如此支持和欣赏真是太好了。当然，我很高兴收到他的消息，它们肯定会对进入周末或之后产生一点影响。”
安东内利还保持着F1最年轻最快圈速、领跑比赛、领跑积分榜和大满贯的纪录，这些纪录是他从刘易斯·汉密尔顿和马克斯·维斯塔潘手中夺走的。
维斯塔潘仍保持着世界锦标赛最年轻车手、积分获得者、登上领奖台和分站冠军的纪录。
补充报道：Ronald Vording和Filip Cleeren
detailEn: Sebastian Vettel: “I’d be very happy” for Kimi Antonelli to beat me as F1’s youngest champion
As Antonelli inches towards a maiden world title, Vettel expects his record to be beaten – and is glad about it
Sebastian Vettel says he will be “very happy” for Kimi Antonelli to beat his record as Formula 1’s youngest world champion.
Vettel earned the accolade in 2010 at 23 years, four months and 11 days old, beating Lewis Hamilton’s 2008 record by five-and-a-half months.

Antonelli is increasingly likely to win this year’s title at just 20 years of age, with his Spanish Grand Prix victory boosting his advantage over main challenger and Mercedes team-mate George Russell to 81 points.
“I'd be very happy for him,” Vettel said in Monza. “He had an incredible year. There's the old phrase that records are there to be broken. He still has a lot of years ahead of him to do so.

“I love the sport, so as a spectator it's very exciting. I'd wish for the others to come back and be more in the mix. I'm independent and happy for [him] because I know how much work there is behind it to achieve it, and whoever will win will deserve it as well.”
Sebastian Vettel winning the 2010 world title in Abu Dhabi

Antonelli has already beaten some records of Vettel’s. The Italian youngster clinched his maiden pole position and his first hat-trick at 19 years old this year, when the German had achieved those feats at 21, back in 2008 and 2009.

The Mercedes driver expressed appreciation for his elder’s encouragement: “It's great. Seb is incredible. He's a friend of mine, always sends some messages after every race weekend or even before some of them.

“It's great to see so much support from him and so much appreciation as well. Definitely, I'm very happy to get his messages, and for sure they make a little difference in going into the weekend or even after.”
Antonelli also holds records as F1’s youngest fastest-lap scorer, race leader, championship leader and grand-chelem achiever, which he snatched away from Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen.
Verstappen retains records as the world championship’s youngest driver, points scorer, podium finisher and race winner.
Additional reporting by Ronald Vording and Filip Cleeren

items.titleZh: F1虚拟安全车规则争议：西班牙站诺里斯事件引发讨论
items.summaryZh: 由于兰多·诺里斯在西班牙大奖赛遭遇的虚拟安全车时机问题，F1虚拟安全车规则预计将被列入体育咨询委员会下次会议议程。
items.originalTitle: F1虚拟安全车规则争议：西班牙站诺里斯事件引发讨论
items.summaryEn: Formula 1's virtual safety car rules are expected to be added to the agenda of the next Sporting Advisory Committee meeting after Lando Norris's experience at the Spanish Grand Prix.
detailZh: 在兰多·诺里斯在西班牙大奖赛上的遭遇之后，一级方程式的虚拟安全车规则即将被提交给车队讨论。
消息人士表示，围绕马德里赛道事件引发的关于虚拟安全车规则的争论意味着，该话题几乎肯定会被列入下一届一级方程式体育咨询委员会（SAC）会议的议程。
在诺里斯本已稳操胜券、有望轻松赢下西班牙大奖赛之际，一次虚拟安全车时段的时机——因赛道上有碎片以及兰斯·斯特罗尔停驶的阿斯顿·马丁赛车——被他形容为“极其倒霉”，并让他付出了代价。
赛事控制中心在诺里斯刚刚驶过维修区入口仅五秒钟后就发布了虚拟安全车，这等于白送了他身后所有追赶的对手一次低成本的进站机会。
然后，更糟糕的是，虚拟安全车在诺里斯自己刚要回到维修区前几秒就结束了，这意味着他为了换胎承受了完整的25秒维修区损失时间。
诺里斯的排名下滑，但他随后的慢速进站并没有影响他的位置。尽管他最终获得第三名，但几乎毫无疑问，如果各车位置在进站过程中得以保持，他本可以赢下比赛。
赛后谈到他觉得这一情况有多么不公时，诺里斯支持让他的经历成为推动虚拟安全车规则可能改革的催化剂。
“这是一条不应该决定比赛结果的规则，”他对天空体育F1说道。“比赛应该由表现最好的人赢下，也许有人在一段（阶段）里冒险跑得更长，也许之后来了一辆安全车，情况就能有所帮助。”
迈凯伦车队领队斯特拉支持他的车手的观点，即西班牙站发生的那些事件——史无前例地暴露出领先车手成为唯一一辆无法在虚拟安全车（VSC）条件下进站的赛车——或许应当促使人们评估规则是否需要修改。
他说：“也许一级方程式界应该进行更广泛的反思，看看是维持现状，还是引入一些能够保持更公平的方式。”
然而，尽管这种情况表面上明显不公，但看起来不太可能达成修改规则的共识，因为旨在拉平差距的各种替代方案过去都已被排除。
对虚拟安全车（VSC）规则的反思看来将在一级方程式的体育咨询委员会（SAC）中进行，该机构由国际汽联代表以及11支车队各自的体育主管组成。
它被用作讨论体育规则问题的论坛，在需要时决定改进措施，并在有足够多车队支持的情况下，与国际汽联共同拟定规则修改的框架。
一旦一项提案通过体育咨询委员会，随后将提交给F1委员会审批，最后还需得到国际汽联世界汽车运动理事会的批准。
体育咨询委员会通常会审查可能存在争议的问题，以确认是否有变革的意愿，而关于虚拟安全车的任何辩论都将属于其职权范围。
然而，任何推动规则修改的行动，很可能都需要所有代表一致认为发生在诺里斯身上的事情是不公平的，而这正是意见可能存在分歧的地方。
虽然迈凯伦和诺里斯肯定会这么想，因为他们是唯一没有机会在虚拟安全车（VSC）期间进站的，但实际上这些事情都是按照既定程序发生的，而这些程序是根据随机出现的事件来执行的。
没有人能预料到斯特罗尔会在20号弯冲上逃生通道。没有人能预料到他会在那条逃生通道里陷住。也没有人能预料到阿隆索和塞恩斯在5号弯发生碰撞，导致赛道上出现碎片，而赛会认为需要清扫这些碎片。
这些事情偏偏在那个时候发生，而虚拟安全车（VSC）程序又紧跟着这些事件启动，对诺里斯来说最多只能算是运气不好——但这并不算不公平。
斯特拉表示，没有任何迹象表明赛会在判定虚拟安全车（VSC）时机时完全基于比赛安全运行的需要而做出任何不当行为。
他认为所发生的事情更多是一种不幸的因素。
“我认为有时候‘倒霉’这个词被用得太多了，但在这种情况下，这几乎是对‘倒霉’的数学定义，”他说。
不过，如果决定对规则进行调整，有几种修改虚拟安全车（VSC）规则的方式。
诺里斯表示，在车手简报会上提到虚拟安全车这个话题时，车手们经常讨论替代方案。
"我们过去谈论过这个问题，谈过好几次，关于如何至少让它在一圈内得到覆盖，或者让每个人都有机会进行进站，"他说。
"或者你干脆封闭进站通道，除了爆胎之类的情况，谁都不能进站。我认为有几件事可以做，让它对所有人来说更简单、更公平，但那是一个更大的讨论。"
虽然斯特拉支持各车队讨论替代性虚拟安全车方案的想法，但他并不确定怎样改进才最好。
他说自己对该怎么做感到"困惑"，随后给出了一个二选一的选择：要么延长每次虚拟安全车时段，让所有赛车都有均等的进站机会，要么照他的话说，"就交给老天爷，有时你运气好，有时你运气不好"。
正如埃德·斯特劳在我们《The 比赛》F1播客的比赛回顾节目中暗示的那样，如果你决定延长虚拟安全车（VSC）时段，让所有车手都有机会进站，最终就会出现这样的局面：赛事控制更关注的是比赛当时如何进行，而不是专注于它的首要职责——保持赛道处于安全状态。
把黄旗状态下的行驶置于绿旗比赛之上，同样是不合逻辑的。
另一种选择是效仿二级方程式（F2）的做法：允许在全安全车出动时进行强制进站，但在虚拟安全车（VSC）期间不允许，这样这种“免费进站”就不会计入你必须完成的轮胎配方更换。
这显然会降低车手在虚拟安全车期间进站的积极性，但它并不一定能消除进站彩票式的运气因素，尤其是当一场比赛需要多次进站，或者这意味着车手可以利用在虚拟安全车期间省下的进站时间，转而采用多次进站策略来获取优势。
这样的改变很可能只是把问题转移到另一个领域，而不是彻底根治。
也许最好的解决方案是，每当虚拟安全车（VSC）出动时，直接关闭维修站。
虚拟安全车（VSC）的设计初衷本来就是在处理赛道上的安全事务时，有效地冻结车与车之间的时间差距。如果一级方程式和国际汽联禁止在这些条件下进行任何进站，那么就不会有人能够在虚拟安全车（VSC）期间获得优势。
这个方案的缺点在于，当虚拟安全车（VSC）出动时，对那些已经进站的车该怎么办：它们是否可以保留这份运气和预判带来的好处，还是应该被留在维修站里，直到虚拟安全车（VSC）结束？
要为虚拟安全车规则找到一个完美的解决方案是一个非常困难的问题，甚至可能根本无解。
而且还有一个来自另一个高水平单座赛车赛事的警示故事，F1 应该引以为鉴——那个赛事曾试图解决这类问题，却失败了。
印地赛车曾决定改变管理黄旗时段的方式，以避免毁掉领跑者的比赛——但事后不得不撤销这些规则。
虽然情况并不完全相同，因为该赛事没有虚拟安全车这一选项，但印地赛车改变了在某些比赛场景下处理安全车时段（称为警报或全赛道警报）的方式，希望避免正是诺里斯在马德里遭遇的那种问题：领跑者因安全车出动的时机而处于不利地位，并失去关键的赛道位置。
detailEn: Formula 1's virtual safety car rules are set to be put up for team discussion in the wake of what happened to Lando Norris at the Spanish Grand Prix.

Sources have suggested that debate over the VSC rules triggered by events at the Madring mean that the topic will almost certainly be added to the agenda of the next meeting of F1's Sporting Advisory Committee (SAC).

Norris looked on course to romp to a straightforward win in Spain before what he referred to as the "insanely unlucky" timing of a VSC period - for debris on track as well as the stopped Aston Martin of Lance Stroll - cost him.
Race control called a VSC just five seconds after Norris had passed the pitlane entry, gifting all his pursing rivals an opportunity for a cheap pitstop.
Then, to make matters worse, the VSC ended just seconds before Norris himself had got back around to the pits, meaning that he endured the full 25-second pitlane time loss for a tyre change.

Norris dropped down the order, with his subsequent slow pitstop not impacting his position. Although he finished third, there was little doubt that he would have won had positions been maintained through the stops.
Speaking after the race about how unfair he felt the situation had been, Norris backed the idea of his experience being a catalyst for potential VSC regulation change.

"It's a rule that shouldn't define a race," he told Sky Sports F1. "A race should be won by the guy who can put in the best performance, who maybe takes a risk by going long in a stint, and maybe you get a safety car later on and things can help."

McLaren team principal Andrea Stella supported his driver's view that perhaps the events of Spain - which were unprecedented in exposing a race leader as being the only car unable to pit under VSC conditions - should serve as a prompt to evaluate whether the regulations need to change.
"Perhaps there's a wider reflection that the F1 community should apply as to whether to keep things like they are or [to] introduce ways of maintaining more fairness," he said.
However, despite the apparent injustice of such a situation, a consensus to change the rules appears unlikely because alternative solutions to even things out have all been ruled out in the past.
Reflection on the VSC looks set to take place in F1's SAC, which is the body composed of FIA representatives and sporting managers from each of F1's 11 teams.

It is used as a forum to discuss issues with sporting regulations, decide on improvements if they are needed, and work through with the FIA the framing of regulation changes if they are supported by enough teams.
Once a proposal has been passed by the SAC it then goes to the F1 Commission for approval, before the final stage of getting ratified by the FIA's World Motor Sport Council.
It is normal for the SAC to review potentially contentious issues to see if there is desire for change, and any debate over the VSC will fall under this remit.
However, any movement to go for a rule change would likely need agreement from every representative that what happened to Norris was unfair, which is an element where opinion may be divided.

While McLaren and Norris will certainly feel that way as the only ones who had no chance to pit under the VSC, in reality these things happen according to mapped out procedures that are implemented based on events that occur randomly.

No one could have predicted Stroll was going to head down the escape road at Turn 20. No one could have predicted he was going to get stuck in that escape road. And no one could have predicted the Turn 5 collision between Fernando Alonso and Carlos Sainz that put debris on the circuit that race control felt needed sweeping up.
That those things happened when they did, and that the VSC procedure followed those events, is at best unlucky for Norris - but it's not unfair.
Stella said there was no suggestion that race control had acted in any way it should not have in judging the timing of the VSC entirely on what was required for the safe operation of the race.
And he suggested what happened was more an element of misfortune.
"I think at times that being unlucky is used for too many applications, but in this case it's almost a mathematical definition of being unlucky," he said.
If, however, it is decided that a rules tweak should be pursued, there are several ways of altering the VSC rules.
Norris said that drivers had regularly discussed alternative solutions when the topic of VSC had come up in drivers' briefings.
"We have spoken about it in the past, several times, about how it can be at least covered for one lap or everyone has the opportunity to do the pitstops," he said.

"Or you just block the pit entry, and no one can box apart from if you have a puncture or something. I think there's a few things you could do to make it more simple and more fair for everyone, but that’s a bigger discussion."
While Stella supported the idea of teams discussing alternative VSC options, he was not certain about how best to improve things.

He said he was "puzzled" about what to do, before presenting a binary choice between extending every VSC period so all cars have equal opportunity to pit, or just leaving it, in his words, "in the hands of the gods and sometimes you're lucky, sometimes you are not".

As Edd Straw suggested in our race review episode of The Race F1 Podcast, if you decide to extend VSC periods so everyone gets a chance to pit, you will end up in a situation where race control is focused more on how the race is playing out at that moment, than simply doing its primary job of keeping the circuit in a safe condition.
It's also nonsensical to prioritise yellow flag running over green flag racing.

Another option would be to follow what Formula 2 does and allow mandatory pitstops under a full safety car but not the VSC, so this kind of 'free pitstop' doesn't count towards your mandated tyre compound switch.

That obviously disincentivises pitting under VSC, but it doesn't necessarily eliminate the pitstop lottery, especially if a race requires multiple stops or it means drivers could gain an advantage by using the pitstop time gained under the VSC to switch to a multi-stop strategy.
Such a change would likely shift the problem to a different area rather than cure it entirely.
Perhaps the best solution would be to simply close the pits whenever a VSC is deployed.

The VSC is already designed to effectively freeze the time gaps between cars while safety matters on track are dealt with. If F1 and the FIA banned any and all pitstops under these conditions, then no one is ever able to gain an advantage under VSC.

The downside with this one is what to do with cars that are already in the pits when the VSC is thrown; do they get to retain the benefit of their good fortune and anticipation, or should they be stuck in the pits until the VSC ends?
A perfect solution to VSC rules is a very difficult problem that may not have a solution.
And there's also a cautionary tale F1 should take note of from another high-level single-seater racing category that tried to tackle this kind of problem and failed.
IndyCar decided to change the way it managed yellow flag periods to avoid ruining leaders' races - and had to undo the rules afterwards.

While it's not quite the same, as that series doesn't have a VSC option, IndyCar made a change to how it dealt with safety car periods - known as cautions or full course cautions - in certain race scenarios, hoping to avoid the exact problem Norris suffered in Madrid: a leader being disadvantaged by the timing of a safety car period and losing crucial track position.

在阿隆索发表评论的第二天，FIA主席穆罕默德·本·苏拉耶姆似乎透露，他希望加速本田的引擎开发，以便他们能够迎头赶上。
"我们绝不能允许费尔南多——阿隆索，一位伟大的冠军——仅仅因为环境而离开。那不是离开舞台的方式，"本·苏拉耶姆说。
"他必须取得成功，然后在他想离开的时候离开，而不是因为性能问题被迫离开。
"我理解这些问题。赛车表现不佳。我周四会见了劳伦斯[·斯特罗尔]，我将进行改革，并与他交谈，让他，试图让他改变主意。这是不可接受的。"

在西班牙大奖赛前，阿隆索讨论他在阿斯顿·马丁和F1的未来。
本·苏拉耶姆补充道："我会和他谈谈。我对他说，我看到他非常难过，我说，'费尔南多，我理解，你来到自己的国家，作为两届世界冠军，现在却排在最后，这是不可接受的。'
"我们在5月早些时候做了一些事情，合法地为车队改进引擎，然后我对他说，'我不会告诉你我们要做什么。请告诉我你想要什么，因为你是车手，来告诉我你想让我们做什么来改善这些结果。'
"突然你看到一切改变，然后我接到一个电话，我和[斯特罗尔]开了会。我们是来支持的。"
阿斯顿·马丁车队领队迈克·克拉克回应关于阿隆索在车队和F1未来的问题。
红牛今年早些时候被FIA认定拥有最好的引擎，尽管围场中大多数人认为梅赛德斯是标杆引擎制造商。
梅赛德斯车队领队托托·沃尔夫和红牛车队领队洛朗·梅基斯对改变持开放态度，以便本田能够迎头赶上。
"在这种情况下，ADUO被设计为一种追赶机制，那个公式对本田解锁了，他们需要更多，"沃尔夫说。
"主席与阿隆索的对话完全合理。我们希望所有这些顶级制造商都留在运动中。我们希望他们具有竞争力并取得成功。
"规则是为了运动的最佳利益，有时可能需要调整，所以对话完全合理。"
卡洛斯·塞恩斯因在马德里与阿隆索发生碰撞而被罚时5秒。
梅基斯补充道："尽管我们不能总是意见一致，但作为一项运动，我们尽量对规则保持相当开放的态度。
"你可能记得，今年早些时候实际上对ADUO规则进行了第一次修改，正是为了帮助那些比最初投票时落后得多的制造商。所有车队都投票支持，我们投了赞成票，为了运动的利益。
"正如我所说，我们不可能在所有事情上达成一致，但作为运动的利益相关者，如果存在需要修复或需要支持的情况，我们通常会找到解决方案。我相信我们会在某个阶段坐下来讨论ADUO规则的未来。我们知道其中的一些不足，我相信以后还有一些需要解决。"
detailEn: Fernando Alonso: What's the latest on Aston Martin driver's future as he weighs up retirement or new contract to stay in F1 in 2027?

Fernando Alonso's future in Formula 1 is up in the air after he revealed news about whether he will remain at Aston Martin will "not come soon".
Alonso has been frustrated with Formula 1's 2026 regulations and the performance of his Aston Martin-Honda car, having scored points just twice this season.

The 45-year-old, whose current contract at Aston Martin expires at the end of this season, suggested how he feels about the power unit tweaks for next year, which will see the electric output reduced from its current near 50 per cent to 42 per cent, will dictate his decision.

"It's a matter of understanding what the rules from next year will have an impact or not on the racing and on the driving side of things," said Alonso last Thursday at the Spanish Grand Prix.
"The current cars, as I said many times, are not the best cars to drive and to enjoy. But next year there is a step in the right direction, hopefully.

"At the same time, I need to think what is the best programme for next year and sit with the team. Behind the wheel or in another role, where I will be helping the most, that will be the most important thing to decide together."
Are FIA set to help Honda to keep Alonso in F1?
A day after Alonso's comments, FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem appeared to reveal he wants to accelerate Honda's engine development so they can catch up.
"There is no way we can allow Fernando to leave - Alonso, a great champion - just because of the circumstances. That's not the way to leave the stage," said Ben Sulayem.
"He has to be successful and then he leaves whenever he wants, not because he was forced to leave because of the performance.

"I share the issues. The car is not performing. I met with Lawrence [Stroll] on Thursday and I'm going to do the changes and will talk to him to make him, try to make him, change his mind. It's not acceptable."
Watch the onboard of Alonso as he's forced to let go of the steering wheel due to vibrations at the Chinese Grand Prix in March

The comments could be seen as a personal intervention by Ben Sulayem but Sky Sports F1 understands the FIA president wants to work with the Power Unit Advisory Committee, which features all five engine manufactures, to work together to help Honda.
One option could be changing the ADUO (Additional Development Upgrades Opportunities) rules to not only be about the ICE (Internal Combustion Engine) power.
Honda have already used one of two engine upgrade opportunities this year, have at least another two for 2027 and were given an extra £14m of development budget.
Ahead of the Spanish Grand Prix, Alonso discusses his future at Aston Martin and in Formula 1

Ben Sulayem added: "I will be speaking to him. I said to him, I saw him very sad, and I said, 'Fernando, I understand, it's not acceptable that you are coming to your own country and now after two times a world champion and you are at the last'.

"We did something earlier, in May, legally for the team towards the engine to go and improve, and then I said to him, 'I am not going to tell you what we are going to do. Please tell me what you want because you are the driver and come and tell me what do you want us to do to improve these results.'
"Suddenly you see everything change, then I get a call and I had a meeting [with Stroll]. We are here to support."
Aston Martin team principal Mike Krack responds to questions regarding Alonso's future in the team and Formula 1
Red Bull were deemed to have the best engine earlier this year by the FIA, although most people in the paddock feel Mercedes are the benchmark engine manufacturer.
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff and Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies are open to changes in order for Honda can catch up.
"The ADUO in that case was designed as a catch-up mechanism and that formula was unlocked for Honda, and they need more," said Wolff.
"And the conversation that the president had with Alonso is fair enough. We want to have all of these top constructors in the sport. We want them to be competitive and successful.
"And regulations are regulations to be for the best of the sport and sometimes maybe they need an adjustment, so fair enough conversation."
Carlos Sainz was given a five-second time penalty for causing a collision with Alonso in Madrid
Mekies added: "As much as we cannot agree all the time, as a sport we try to keep a fairly open look at the regulations.

"You may recall that actually there was a first change in the ADUO regulations done earlier this year precisely in order to help those who were much behind, compared to what was initially voted. All the teams voted that, we voted in favour of that for the benefit of the sport.

"As I said, we cannot agree on everything but certainly as stakeholders of the sport if there is a situation that needs to be fixed or needs to be supported, we normally find solutions. And I'm sure that we will at some stage sit down and discuss the future of the ADUO regulations. The shortfalls, we know some of them, and I'm sure there is a few of those to address later on."

detailZh: 安德烈亚·斯特拉：迈凯伦必须帮助奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里停止对如何驾驶2026款F1赛车进行“思考”
迈凯伦表示将支持皮亚斯特里，帮助他与MCL40 F1赛车找到更自然的平衡
迈凯伦车队领队安德烈亚·斯特拉认为，奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里目前落后于兰多·诺里斯，原因在于这位澳大利亚车手仍在“一边思考一边驾驶”2026款F1赛车。
皮亚斯特里对新一代F1赛车的不适应在本赛季至今已显而易见。过去两年已经清楚表明，他的优势在于在高速弯中保持速度以及在抓地力较高的条件下发挥。2026款规则带来的空气动力学输出降低和更窄的轮胎，使新车的抓地力大幅减少，让皮亚斯特里脱离了整体的舒适区。
这一点，加上2026款动力单元的“充能-释放”特性，共同导致了皮亚斯特里本赛季至今的艰难处境。尽管他和诺里斯在2025赛季全年都极为接近，但除了赛季末低抓地力赛道的几场比赛外，诺里斯在今年一直占据明显优势。
斯特拉表示，如果迈凯伦能够让皮亚斯特里在赛道上停止“思考”，他将有所提升，并承认驾驶今年的MCL40对这位墨尔本车手来说并非一个自然的过程。
“我认为对奥斯卡来说，我们需要排位赛做得更好，从一开始就更接近领奖台位置，”斯特拉开始说道。“在蒙扎，他在排位赛结束时是P3，但由于阻挡，我们不知怎么地只能从P6起步。所以有几种情况我们需要更好地掌控。”
“我们需要更好地执行，同时我们需要让奥斯卡与MCL40更加协调，因为奥斯卡仍然在一边驾驶一边思考。当你一边驾驶一边思考时，事情会变慢；作为车手，决定该做什么的速度会变慢，最终你的圈速也会变慢。”
“所以我认为需要改进的议程非常明确，我期望，就像我一直说的那样，我们会解决这个问题，我们会在（赛季）最后阶段看到一个更强大的奥斯卡。”
皮亚斯特里在第一弯与乔治·拉塞尔的梅赛德斯接触后前翼受损，导致襟翼在端板旁晃动。
斯特拉表示，迈凯伦担心这对皮亚斯特里前轮的影响，但硬胎足够耐用，确保他没有出现颗粒化，因此无需更换前翼。他甚至在进站后超越了阿尔维德·林德布拉德，但最终被困在弗兰科·科拉平托的阿尔派之后，以第七名完赛。
“前翼损坏让奥斯卡损失了几个单位的气动平衡，”斯特拉补充道。“所以绝对是非常可测量的。”
“我们其实相当担心这会导致大量颗粒化，因为前部失去了很多下压力。事实上，幸运的是，硬胎足够硬且耐用，没有出现颗粒化，所以奥斯卡能够留在比赛中。”
“就奥斯卡而言，我认为这场比赛肯定受到了影响，不仅是因为赛车受损，还因为在起步时又失去了位置。所以我认为即使没有损坏，在他所处的境况下也很难从中获得更多。”
detailEn: Andrea Stella: McLaren must help Oscar Piastri stop "thinking" about how to drive '26 F1 car
McLaren says it will support Piastri in helping to find a more natural balance with its MCL40 F1 car
McLaren team principal Andrea Stella believes Oscar Piastri's current deficit to Lando Norris is down to the Australian still "thinking and driving" with the 2026 Formula 1 machinery.

Piastri's discomfort with the new breed of F1 cars has been evident throughout the season so far. It had become clear over the previous two years that his strengths lie in carrying speed through high-speed corners and in high-grip conditions. The reduced aero output and narrower tyres dictated by the 2026 rules have stripped away much of the grip from the new cars, bringing Piastri out of his overall comfort zone.

This, allied to the charge-and-deploy nature of the '26 powertrains, has contributed to Piastri's tough year thus far. While he and Norris were incredibly close across the course of 2025, aside from the lower-grip races among the final flyaways, Norris has held a clear advantage through this year.

Stella says that Piastri will improve if McLaren is able to stop him from "thinking" while on-track, and accepts that driving this year's MCL40 does not feel like a natural process for the Melburnian.

"I think with Oscar we need to qualify better, stay closer to the podium finish positions from the start," Stella began. "In Monza he was P3 at the end of qualifying but somehow we managed to start P6 for the impeding. So there are several circumstances of which we need to take more control.

"We need to execute better and then at the same time we need to get more in tune between Oscar and the MCL40 because still Oscar is driving and thinking. And when you drive and think, things get slowed down; slower as a driver in terms of deciding what to do and ultimately you are slower in terms of lap times.
"So I think the agenda is very clear as to what we have to improve and I expect, like I always say, that we will get on top of that and we will see a stronger Oscar in the final part [of the year]."
Piastri suffered front wing damage in the first corner after encountering George Russell's Mercedes, which left the diveplane flapping around against the endplate.

Stella says that McLaren was concerned about the impact on Piastri's front tyres, but the hard compound was durable enough to ensure that he experienced no graining - thus not necessitating a front wing change. He even managed to put a pass on Arvid Lindblad after his pitstop, but ended up becoming trapped behind Franco Colapinto's Alpine to finish seventh.
"The front wing damage cost Oscar a few units of aero balance," Stella added. "So definitely very measurable.

"We were actually quite worried that this would have caused a lot of graining because the front end lost a lot of downforce. As a matter of fact, and thankfully, the hard tyres were hard and resistant enough not to open up the graining so Oscar could stay in the race.

"When it comes to Oscar, I think the race was definitely compromised by not only the damage on the car but having lost further positions at the start. So I think even without the damage, it would have been a difficult race to get more out of the situation in which he found himself."

2026款动力单元的“充能-释放”特性也加剧了皮亚斯特里本赛季的困难。
在蒙扎，皮亚斯特里因阻挡被罚，排位赛P3却从P6起步；正赛首圈与乔治·拉塞尔的梅赛德斯接触导致前翼受损，最终以第七名完赛。

items.summaryZh: 法拉利领队弗雷德·瓦塞尔表示，尽管夺冠希望日渐渺茫，车队仍将继续研发SF-26赛车，暂不转向2027年项目。

items.originalTitle: 法拉利暂不将重心转向2027年F1赛车
items.summaryEn: Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur says the team will keep developing its SF-26 F1 car despite diminishing title chances, rather than switching focus to the 2027 car yet.
detailZh: 法拉利为何还不把重心转向2027年F1赛车
尽管夺冠希望越来越渺茫，法拉利仍打算继续升级SF-26
法拉利车队领队弗雷德·瓦塞尔表示，尽管争夺冠军的可能性正在减小，车队仍将继续研发其SF-26一级方程式赛车。
在刘易斯·汉密尔顿因刹车问题从西班牙大奖赛退赛之后，这位七届世界冠军在车手积分榜上已经落后领跑者基米·安东内利101分。与此同时，夏尔·勒克莱尔在马德里赛道仅获得第四名，这意味着法拉利在车队积分榜上落后梅赛德斯145分。
在成本上限和空气动力学测试限制的背景下，赛车研发资源必须谨慎分配；在引擎方面，法拉利已经推出了它被允许进行的两项ADUO升级。
虽然各车队都在研发2027年的新赛车，但瓦塞尔并不打算让法拉利就此把全部精力放在这上面。
“我们现在的情况和12个月前不一样，”这位法国人谈到2026年F1规则大改时说，“如今我们所研发的东西，将能够延续到明年的项目上。我们会继续工作，但也许是针对不同的东西、不同的方面。
“我们现在所做的研发，80%都将被延续使用。”
就法拉利的夺冠前景而言，瓦塞尔被问到现在对安东内利和梅赛德斯来说是否已经'大势已去'——他拒绝直接回答这个问题。
'两三周前我告诉过你们，我会一场比赛一场比赛地看。我没有改变，'他坚持说。
法拉利的关键可能在于排位赛表现，因为夏休期以来的四节排位赛（包括赞德沃特冲刺赛）中，汉密尔顿和勒克莱尔都没能排进前排。他们的平均位置是第五，SF-26 赛车与杆位成绩的差距为 0.198 秒——比迈凯伦和梅赛德斯慢，比红牛快。
'这是我们需要改进的地方，因为我认为你看比赛节奏的话，正赛中的节奏是有的，'瓦塞尔说。'当然我们需要在排位赛中做得更好。'
“如果把赞德福特站和这一站放在一起看，这两站比赛的赛事特点对我们来说有点相似。我们在排位赛中速度还不错，但在最后一圈没有把所有东西都发挥出来，正赛节奏也还可以。
“如果今天必须让车队聚焦于某件事，那就是排位赛中节奏的演进——不仅仅是排位赛本身的节奏，而是这种演进，你能做到的每一步进步。我们在Q3第一组圈速时就已经有竞争力了，潜力是存在的，我们只需要在后续进一步把所有东西都调整到位。”
detailEn: Why Ferrari won't switch focus to 2027 F1 car yet
Despite its title chances growing slimmer, Ferrari intends to keep updating the SF-26
Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur says the Scuderia will keep developing its SF-26 Formula 1 car, despite its diminishing title chances.

After Lewis Hamilton retired from the Spanish Grand Prix with brake issues, the seven-time world champion is 101 points adrift of championship leader Kimi Antonelli in the drivers’ standings. Meanwhile, Charles Leclerc finished just fourth at Madring, meaning Ferrari is 145 points down on Mercedes in the constructors’.

Car development resources have to be carefully allocated in light of the cost cap and the aerodynamic testing restrictions; engine-wise, Ferrari has already introduced the two ADUO upgrades it has been allowed.
While teams are known to be working on their 2027 challengers, Vasseur has no intention to make that Ferrari’s full focus just yet.

“We are not in the situation of 12 months ago,” the Frenchman said, referring to F1’s regulatory overhaul for 2026. “Today, what we will develop, we will be able to carry it over on next year's project. We will continue to work, but perhaps on different things, different aspects.
“The development that we do now, 80% will be carried over.”
As far as Ferrari’s title chances are concerned, Vasseur was asked if it was now ‘game over’ against Antonelli and Mercedes – a question he refused to answer directly.
“Two or three weeks ago I told you that I will take race by race. I didn't change,” he insisted.

The key for Ferrari may be qualifying performance, as Hamilton and Leclerc have both failed to qualify on the front row in any of the four sessions (Zandvoort sprint included) since the summer break. Their average position is fifth, and the SF-26’s deficit to pole has been 0.198s – slower than McLaren and Mercedes, quicker than Red Bull.
“This we need to improve, because I think when you have a look on the pace, during the race the pace is there,” Vasseur said. “For sure we need to do a better job in quali.

“If you take Zandvoort and this one, the profile of the event is a little bit the same for us. We had a decent pace in quali, but we didn't put everything together on the last attempt, and race pace is OK.

“If I have to put the focus of the team on something today, it would be the evolution of the pace during the quali – more than the pace in quali, the evolution, the steps that you can do. We were there on run one Q3, the potential is there, we just have to adapt everything further on.”

items.summaryEn: McLaren team principal Andrea Stella said overtaking was too difficult at the Madring for Lando Norris to win the Spanish Grand Prix. Norris took pole and pulled six seconds clear in the first 12 laps, but was too far ahead to pit under the virtual safety car and, despite closing on Kimi Antonelli and Max Verstappen, was never able to make a move.
detailZh: 兰多·诺里斯因马德里赛道无法超车而错失F1胜利——迈凯伦
如果超车更容易，安德烈亚·斯特拉相信诺里斯本可以赢得西班牙大奖赛
马克斯·维斯塔潘，红牛车队；兰多·诺里斯，迈凯伦
迈凯伦F1车队领队安德烈亚·斯特拉表示，马德里赛道的超车过于困难，兰多·诺里斯因此无法赢得西班牙大奖赛。
诺里斯在马德里新街道赛道夺得杆位，并在比赛前12圈拉开6秒差距，但这反而成为他的隐患——虚拟安全车出动时他距离太远，无法进站。
在耗时七秒的换胎后，诺里斯发现自己落后基米·安东内利16秒。到第48圈时，他已追近这位意大利车手和排名第二的马克斯·维斯塔潘，但始终无法完成超越。
因此斯特拉认为，那次慢进站并没有改变诺里斯的结果。“因为兰多很可能无论如何都会（出站后）落在（乔治）拉塞尔后面，”他指出。“而且即使不是这样，也不可能超越维斯塔潘和安东内利。
“所以，我们肯定注意到，我们的操作还有很多工作要做。而且这已经不是我们第一次进站缓慢了。但就比赛本身而言，这并没有造成影响。”
马德里赛道或许难辞其咎。周日的正赛仅出现10次超车，是2026赛季至今最少的——甚至少于摩纳哥的11次。在这10次中，有4次是瓦尔特利·博塔斯或兰斯·斯特罗尔在队尾被超越。
尼科·霍肯伯格，奥迪F1车队；兰斯·斯特罗尔，阿斯顿·马丁
5号弯是刹车最重的区域，但紧接一个弯道，使刹车更难把握，而且弯道太窄，难以轻松完成动作。
“说到超车，这么困难真是遗憾，”斯特拉补充道。“这需要非常大的、非常大的圈速差距才能超车。我认为F1必须审视这条赛道是否需要一些修改，以引入超车的可能性。
“因为目前的事实是，直道或许足够长，但两辆车绝对不可能一起进入5号弯。所以超车尝试基本上是不可能的——这有点遗憾，因为我认为如果今天能超车，我们本会看到兰多重新夺回领先，因为速度优势非常明显。”
detailEn: Lando Norris lost Madring F1 win because of impossible overtaking – McLaren
Had overtaking been easier, Andrea Stella believes Norris could have won the Spanish GP
Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Lando Norris, McLaren
McLaren Formula 1 team principal Andrea Stella says overtaking was too difficult at the Madring for Lando Norris to win the Spanish Grand Prix.

Norris took pole position at Madrid’s new street circuit and pulled away by six seconds in the first 12 laps of the race, which proved to be his downfall as he was too far ahead to pit when the virtual safety car was called.

After a seven-second tyre change, Norris found himself 16 seconds adrift of Kimi Antonelli. By lap 48 he had bridged the gap to the Italian and second-placed Max Verstappen, but never was able to make a move.

Stella therefore believes the slow stop made no difference to Norris’ result. “Because probably Lando would have [come out] anyhow behind [George] Russell,” he pointed out. “And even if not, it would have not been possible to overtake Verstappen and Antonelli.
“So, definitely, we take note that there's a lot of work to do in our operation. And it's not the first time that we have a slow stop. But in terms of the race itself, it didn't make a difference.”

The Madring track might be to blame. Sunday’s race featured just 10 overtaking moves, the least of the 2026 season so far – even fewer than Monaco, which had 11. Of those 10, four consisted in Valtteri Bottas or Lance Stroll getting passed at the back of the pack.
Nico Hulkenberg, Audi F1 Team, Lance Stroll, Aston Martin
Turn 5 was the heaviest braking zone but followed a curve, which made braking trickier, and was too narrow to allow for easy manoeuvres.

“When it comes to overtaking, it's a shame that it's so difficult,” Stella added. “It just requires a large, large lap time difference to be able to overtake. I think what F1 will have to review is whether there are some modifications required at this circuit in order to introduce an overtaking possibility.

“Because at the moment, the fact is that the straight may be long enough, but there's absolutely no way that two cars can enter [Turn] 5 together. So it's basically impossible an attempt of overtaking – which is a bit of a shame, because I think if overtaking was possible today, we would have [had] Lando regaining the lead, because the pace advantage was significant.”
keyPointsZh: 诺里斯进站耗时七秒，出站后落后安东内利16秒，第48圈追至安东内利和维斯塔潘身后但未能超越。
斯特拉认为慢进站没有影响结果，因为诺里斯无论如何都可能落在拉塞尔身后，且无法超越维斯塔潘和安东内利。
周日正赛仅出现10次超车，为2026赛季至今最少，甚至少于摩纳哥的11次；其中4次是博塔斯或斯特罗尔在队尾被超越。

items.originalTitle: 这一'修复'方案本无法拯救F1西班牙大奖赛
items.summaryEn: The lack of overtaking at the Madring circuit has been blamed for the Spanish Grand Prix's poor spectacle, but another overlooked factor was the lack of strategic variation, meaning track changes alone would not have saved the race.
detailZh: 西班牙大奖赛未能呈现出今年其他一级方程式比赛所提供的那种精彩场面，这不可避免地让人们把焦点放在了马德里赛道缺乏超车机会这一点上。
组合式弯道、护栏收窄点以及缺乏宽阔的重刹车区域——尤其是在5号弯——都使得超越对手变得极其困难。
正如The 比赛（比赛媒体）在周日透露的那样，马德里赛道的主管方已经在计划对三个关键弯角进行改造，以迎接2027年，并期待明年的比赛能呈现出更多看点，这也就不足为奇了。
但导致比赛缺乏精彩对抗的不仅仅是赛道布局，另一个影响比赛走向的因素是战略上的变化也不多。
再无聊的赛道布局，只要轮胎策略被彻底打乱，也能奉献精彩的对决。
如果通往方格旗的最快路线变得不明确，各车队就会采取不同的策略，同时由此产生的速度差也会制造出并轮缠斗的机会。
马德里赛道就出现了那种摩纳哥或索契式的现象：硬胎（在西班牙站是C2配方）足够支撑整场比赛——加斯利就证明了这一点，他一直坚持到倒数第二圈才进行强制配方更换，换掉他起步时使用的轮胎。
周五首次练习后，鉴于观察到的高磨损程度，曾有人半开玩笑地称可能出现六停策略；但随后情况戏剧性地转变为轻松的一停，令人惊讶。
哈斯车手奥康表示，轮胎的表现是导致比赛中没有太多精彩对抗的限制因素之一，因为只要车手不在前车尾流中待太久，就可以毫无顾虑地持续推进。
他说：“问题在于第二节 阶段（节段）轮胎表现得太稳定了，一旦你跟上前车，你就会损失大量抓地力。”
“当我给其他车让蓝旗的时候，我轻松就损失了半秒，甚至十分之七秒。之后抓地力又会恢复，因为这完全和过热有关。”
“一旦过热降下来，你的速度就回来了。所以这就是为什么没有超车。基本上来说，节奏太快了。”
“从你进站的那一刻到最后，简直就是120%的状态。而且因为没出现颗粒化，我们才取得了这样的结果。如果我们周五就有一场比赛，情况会好得多！”
这样的结果不可避免地引发了质疑：如果轮胎配方更偏激进一些，马德里赛道这场大戏会不会更精彩？
一个美好的设想是：如果去掉C2硬胎在耐热性和机械耐磨性上带来的那份从容，西班牙大奖赛本来会更好看。
这意味着，如果被迫使用更软的配方，车手们在轮胎撑不完全程的情况下会面临更大挑战，从而带来更多刺激。
这个想法不错，但遗憾的是，现实很残酷，因为要理解决定一场比赛能否成为策略杰作的种种复杂因素并不容易。
首先，C2 和 C3 在表现和特性上有明显差异，这意味着虽然硬胎适合跑完整场比赛，中性胎的表现却明显差得多，而且更容易出现轮胎起粒的风险。
正如迈凯伦的皮亚斯特里所说：“中性胎简直糟透了。它实际上只在一圈内表现不错，之后就非常糟糕。”
不过，轮胎衰退加剧并不自动意味着进站次数更多。它可能导致（尤其是在超车困难时）更多的轮胎管理和赛车远远偏离节奏，最终呈现的场面就和周日的比赛一样。
此外，马德里赛道有一个重要因素将永远不利于多次进站的比赛，那就是维修区通道的长度。
在那里更换轮胎大约需要25秒——这是本赛季损失时间最大的赛道之一——所以车队总是想尽量减少换胎的必要性。
根据马德里赛道的实际情况，倍耐力认为把配方调软一档——使用C3/C4/C5而不是C2/C3/C4——并不能提升比赛的观赏性。
这是因为，正如倍耐力赛车运动负责人达里奥·马拉富斯基所指出的，从车手们在比赛中短暂使用C3和C4轮胎时苦苦支撑的表现来看，那样做只会把比赛变成一场艰难的轮胎管理大戏。
再加上马德里赛道凭借倾斜的La Monumental弯道以及大量的弯角，成为赛历中对轮胎要求最具挑战性的赛道之一，这也会因高磨损程度而增加安全风险的可能性。
“这将是一场因高磨损而需要两次进站的比赛，”马拉法斯基对The 比赛表示，“从纸面上看，你可以说‘好吧，这必须是一次两次进站的比赛’。”
“但由于交通状况的影响，车手们最终只会像加斯利那样做。”
“把C2作为比赛用胎是个好选择，这让车队在早期安全车出现的情况下仍有可能一次进站完成比赛。如果用C3/C4/C5就太过分了。”
如果再选择更软的轮胎，排位赛也会出现麻烦。实际上，使用C4轮胎的车队在争夺发车位时，仅仅跑一个单圈冲刺，轮胎就因过热而发出尖啸。
C5轮胎很可能会性能断崖式下滑，基本没什么用处。
马拉富斯基补充道："即使用软胎只跑一圈，经过纪念性弯道（La Monumental）之后，后轮过热的问题就已经出现了。如果软胎是C5，也许在排位赛中也会有热衰退的风险。那就得不偿失了。"
现实情况是，一场比赛能呈现多种策略并行的完美组合、还是变成毫无悬念的轻松一停，抑或陷入彻底混乱，三者之间的差距有时并不大。
由于马德里赛道非常平整、抓地力很高，各车队在赛前就清楚，只要能避免轮胎起粒的风险，一停策略就是可行的。
如果不能避免，正如一位工程师所说，比赛就会变成一场混乱、轮胎严重衰退、两停甚至更多次进站的起粒大混战。
虽然后者听起来很刺激，但实际上它同样有风险，会带来一样糟糕的结果：那就是那种进站循环没完没了、整场比赛毫无叙事线索的大奖赛。
马德里赛道一些注定的特点——平整且高抓地力的表面、La Monumental弯角所承受的巨大作用力、以及很长的维修区通道——意味着除非超车机会得到改善，否则很难通过其他手段鼓励更多的进站。
所有人的目光都集中在明年赛道会做出哪些改动上，因为为超车打开大门，也将是提升比赛策略性元素的最佳方式。
detailEn: The failure of the Spanish Grand Prix to produce the kind of spectacle offered by other Formula 1 races this year has inevitably focused on the lack of overtaking opportunities around the Madring circuit.
Combined entries, barrier pinch points and a lack of wide, heavy braking zones - especially at Turn 5 - all contributed to making it extremely difficult to pass a rival.

It is little wonder, as The Race revealed on Sunday, that Madring chiefs are already planning changes to three key corners for 2027 with the expectation that next year's race produces a bit more of a show.
But it was not just the track layout that contributed to a lack of action, as another factor in how things played out was that there was not much strategic variation either.
Even the most boring of track layouts can deliver thrillers if tyre strategy gets blown open.
Make the fastest route to the chequered flag unclear and you get teams taking different approaches, plus the kinds of pace offset that create the circumstances for wheel-to-wheel action.

The Madring delivered one of those Monaco/Sochi-style phenomena where the hard tyre (the C2 compound in Spain) was good enough to last the whole race - as Pierre Gasly proved by waiting until the penultimate lap for his mandatory compound switch to get off what he had started the race with.

After tongue-in-cheek claims after first running on Friday of a potential six-stopper being on the cards, based on the high levels of degradation seen, the transformation into an easy one-stopper was remarkable.

Haas driver Esteban Ocon said the behaviour of the tyres was one of the limiting factors in why there was not much action in the race, because drivers could push on without fear of excessive degradation as long as they did not spend too much time in the dirty air of the car ahead.
"The thing is that it was so consistent, the tyres on the second stint, that as soon as you were following another car, you were losing so much grip," he said.
"When I was doing blue flags to other cars, I was losing half a second, seven tenths easily. And then after it was coming back because it was all about overheating.
"As soon as the overheating was coming down, you had pace again. So that's why there was no overtaking. It was too fast, the pace, basically.
"It was like 120% from as soon as you pitted to the end. And because the graining didn't happen, that's where we ended up. If we had a race on Friday, it would have been much better!"
This outcome has inevitably prompted questions about whether the Madring spectacle would have been more entertaining had the tyre compounds been a bit more on the aggressive side.
It is a nice theory that if you took away the comfort of the thermal and mechanical robustness of the C2 hard tyre the Spanish GP would have been better.
That suggests that, forced onto softer compounds, drivers would have had a more challenging time in having rubber that did not last the whole distance, thereby producing more excitement.
The idea is good, but sadly reality bites when it comes to understanding the complex factors that dictate whether races become strategic masterclasses.

First, there is a notable difference in behaviour and characteristics between the C2 and the C3, which means that, while the hard was good for the whole race, the medium was significantly not as good and much more prone to the risk of graining.
As McLaren's Oscar Piastri said: "The medium tyre was just awful. It was good for literally one lap, but then it was terrible."

Increased degradation does not automatically mean more stops though. It can (especially when overtaking is difficult) lead to more tyre management and cars running well off the pace, and you end up with the same spectacle as we got on Sunday.
Plus, one important element at Madring that will forever speak against multi-stop races is the length of the pitlane.
Swapping tyres there costs around 25 seconds - one of the biggest losses of the season - so teams are always going to try to minimise the need to change tyres.
Based on the evidence from the Madring, Pirelli felt that going a step softer with the compounds - bringing the C3/C4/C5 rather than the C2/C3/C4 - was not a way to improve the spectacle.

That is because, as Pirelli's head of motorsport, Dario Marrafuschi, pointed out, based on the struggles that drivers had with the C3 and C4 in the short stints in which they managed to keep them alive in the race, it would have simply turned the race into a major management drama.

Throw into the mix too that the Madring, thanks to the banked La Monumental and high numbers of corners, is one of the most challenging tracks on the calendar for tyres, then it would also increase the possibility of safety dangers thanks to the high levels of wear.
"It would have been a two-stop race with a high wear," Marrafuschi told The Race. "On paper you can say, 'OK, it must be a two-stopper'.
"But, because of traffic, drivers would just end up doing what Gasly did.
"It was a good choice to have the C2 as a race compound and give teams the possibility to have one-stop in case of an early safety car. The C3/C4/C5 would have been too much."
Going softer would also have caused trouble in qualifying. As it was, the C4 teams took into the fight for grid positions was screaming from overheating doing a single push lap.
The C5 would probably have fallen off a cliff and been pretty useless.

Marrafuschi added: "Even during one lap with the soft, after La Monumental, the overheating of the rear was there. If the soft was a C5, maybe you would run the risk of thermal degradation during qualifying as well. It wouldn't pay the bill."
The reality is that the margins between a race delivering a perfect strategy mix of different approaches, a nailed on easy one-stopper, and complete chaos are sometimes not very much.
With Madrid's track being super-smooth, and offering high grip, teams knew going into the race that if they could avoid the risk of graining, then the one-stop strategy was on.
If not, as one engineer said, then it would instead have turned into a chaotic, heavy-degradation, two-stop-plus graining fest.
While the latter may sound exciting, it actually risks producing something that is equally as bad: one of those grands prix where there is just an endless cycle of stops so the race has no narrative.

Some of the nailed-on elements of Madring - the smooth, high-grip surface, the forces through La Monumental, and the long pitlane - mean that unless overtaking opportunities are improved there is little that can be done to encourage more stops.
All eyes are on what track changes are done next year because opening the door for passes will be the best way to improve the strategy element too.

items.summaryZh: 尼科·罗斯伯格认为，乔治·拉塞尔目前可能正被一种类似当年他试图扭转对刘易斯·汉密尔顿连败局面时的“疯狂动力”所驱动，以在与基米·安东内利的竞争中扭转局势。
items.originalTitle: 罗斯伯格：拉塞尔或正以“疯狂动力”应对安东内利的挑战
items.summaryEn: Nico Rosberg believes George Russell is likely being driven by a similar "insane motivation" to turn the tables on Kimi Antonelli as he once was to get the better of Lewis Hamilton after recurring defeats.
detailZh: 乔治·拉塞尔：梅赛德斯车手输给基米·安东内利将感到“痛苦”，尼科·罗斯伯格如是说，同时这位车手被看好将迎来突破

尼科·罗斯伯格认为，乔治·拉塞尔目前将受到类似程度的“疯狂动力”驱动，以扭转对基米·安东内利的局面，就像他当年在反复失利后要战胜刘易斯·汉密尔顿一样。
拉塞尔今年首次成为世界冠军的希望日益渺茫，状态正佳的梅赛德斯队友安东内利在积分榜榜首将领先优势扩大到81分。
自从赢得3月的赛季揭幕战澳大利亚大奖赛后，季前夺冠热门拉塞尔在两人均完赛的最近10场比赛中仅两次领先安东内利，这位英国人目睹这位年轻的意大利人在蒙扎-马德里背靠背比赛中拿下本赛季第七和第八场胜利。

周日的比赛后，拉塞尔获得第五名，罗斯伯格在天空体育 F1上被问及他当年在2016年从被梅赛德斯队友汉密尔顿彻底击败后反弹赢得世界冠军的经历。
“我很大程度上是被痛苦所驱动，”罗斯伯格回忆道。
“主观上，不断输给刘易斯是痛苦的，而这恰恰驱动了一种疯狂的动力。
“乔治将处于类似的情况。他现在会如此拼命地想要找到提升。
“他会非常努力，因为我知道乔治不会放弃，他讨厌被基米一次又一次击败的局面。
“他会超级努力，但这有点困难，因为很难理解他的速度去哪了。”
2026年西班牙大奖赛集锦
拉塞尔在梅赛德斯的前四个赛季中有三个赛季是车队得分最高的车手，其中三年里两次胜过汉密尔顿（2022年和2024年），一次与新人安东内利搭档（2025年），但今年要想再次做到这一点，他需要重大逆转，因为赛历上还剩九场比赛。
罗斯伯格相信，勤奋的拉塞尔会继续努力，在W17赛车上找到突破，尽管他说这位28岁的车手不可避免地也会自我怀疑。
“我对乔治的方式印象深刻，因为他确实是个完美主义者，他试图涵盖人类表现的每一个方面，”这位天空体育 F1评论员补充道。
“我知道他在竭尽所能，我钦佩这一点。
“但正因如此，这对他更难，因为他自己也不理解。他一直很快；他一直至少与队友持平，突然之间这在他那里消失了。
“这真的很痛苦，因为你开始怀疑自己。无论你多么自信，然后就会[质疑]‘我是不是不够好？我过去是不是更好，而现在只是做错了什么？’这真的很难。”

“实际上我不在争夺中”——拉塞尔几乎排除车手冠军可能
就在前一周在蒙扎被安东内利夺走胜利（尽管队友因罚退从第19位发车）而落后66分之后，拉塞尔在进入西班牙大奖赛周末时承认，他今年要实现冠军梦“需要一些运气”。
在马德里赛道对他而言令人失望的周末，这一差距扩大到赛季最高的81分，这个周末因排位赛Q3的困难以及正赛中早早出现的虚拟安全车而受到影响。这一结果导致拉塞尔在周日晚上几乎将自己排除在争夺之外。
在评估自己对即将到来的比赛（从9月24日至26日的阿塞拜疆大奖赛开始）的策略时，拉塞尔告诉F1：“继续推进。尽管今天的成绩远非理想，但最近几场比赛更为积极。
“但这差不多就是本赛季的写照。我只需要专注于表现，继续努力帮助车队。
“我们显然处于赢得车队冠军的有利位置，实际上我已不在车手冠军的争夺中，这让我能够只专注于一场一场地比赛，努力专注于取得一些好成绩。”
梅赛德斯副领队布拉德利·洛德和乔治·拉塞尔讨论车队如何通过青训项目支持年轻人才，并资助基层可持续燃料项目
“我们只需把它释放出来”——沃尔夫支持“顶级车手”拉塞尔找到突破
他的梅赛德斯车队仍然相信拉塞尔会找回最佳状态。
当被问及拉塞尔目前最艰难地在为什么而战时，梅赛德斯车队领队托托·沃尔夫说：“我不知道，因为你能看到他在最后追赶勒克莱尔时的速度。他是赛道上最快的。
“但在换胎之后，速度就不在了。
“我就是不知道它在哪里，我们必须分析，因为显然它就在他身上，就在车里，我们只需把它释放出来。”

Nico Rosberg believes George Russell will currently be driven by a similar level of "insane motivation" to turn the tables on Kimi Antonelli as he was to get the better of Lewis Hamilton after recurring defeats.
Russell's hopes of becoming world champion for the first time this year are increasingly slim with in-form Mercedes team-mate Antonelli opening an 81-point lead over him at the top of the standings.

Since winning March's season-opening Australian Grand Prix, pre-season title favourite Russell has only twice finished ahead of Antonelli in the last 10 races they have both completed with the Briton seeing the young Italian take his seventh and eighth wins of the season across the Monza-Madrid double header.

Rosberg was asked after Sunday's race, in which Russell finished fifth, on Sky Sports F1 about his experience of rebounding to win his world title in 2016 after being soundly beaten to the crown by Mercedes team-mate Hamilton the year before.
"I was driven a lot by the pain," recalled Rosberg.
"Subjectively, it was painful to keep losing against Lewis and that just drove an insane motivation.
"George will be in a similar situation. He will be so damn motivated at the moment to try and find improvements.
"He'll be working so hard because I know George doesn't give up and he's hating the situation of getting beaten over and over by Kimi.
"He'll be working super hard but it's a bit of a difficult one because it's hard to understand where the pace has gone for him."

Russell has been Mercedes' top-scoring driver in three of his previous four seasons at the team, twice in three years against Hamilton (2022 and 2024) and once alongside a rookie Antonelli (2025), but he requires a major turnaround for that to be the case again this year with nine scheduled races left.
Rosberg believes the diligent Russell will keep working away to find a breakthrough with the W17 car, although says it is inevitable that the 28-year-old will be questioning himself too.
"I'm very impressed with George's approach because he's really a perfectionist and he tries to cover every aspect of his human performance," added the Sky Sports F1 pundit.
"I know he's doing everything he can, and I admire that.
"But, all the more, it's tough for him because he doesn't understand himself. He's always been fast; he's always been at least level with his team-mate and suddenly it's gone away from him there.

"It's really painful because you start to doubt yourself. It doesn't matter how confident you are, it then comes [to questioning] 'am I not good enough? Was I better in the past and I'm just doing something wrong now?' It's really difficult."
Sky Sports News' Craig Slater reflects on all the big talking points after the Spanish Grand Prix
'Realistically I'm not in the fight' - Russell all-but rules out drivers' title win

Fresh from being beaten to victory by Antonelli the weekend before at Monza despite his team-mate starting a penalised 19th on the grid to fall 66 points off the pace, Russell conceded going into the Spanish Grand Prix weekend that he would "need some luck" to realise his title dreams this year.

That deficit grew to a season-high 81 points in a disappointing weekend for him at the Madring, which was compromised by a difficult Q3 in qualifying and then an early Virtual Safety Car in the race. That result led to Russell all but ruling himself out of contention on Sunday evening.

Assessing his approach for the forthcoming races, starting with the Azerbaijan Grand Prix on September 24-26, Russell told F1: "Just keep pushing along. It has been a more positive couple of races even though the result was far from great today.
"But it's kind of story of the season. I just need to focus on the performance, keep trying to help the team.

"We're obviously in a great place to win the constructors', realistically I'm not in the fight for the drivers', and that just allows me just to focus on race-by-race and trying to focus on getting some good results."
Mercedes deputy team principal Bradley Lord and George Russell discuss how the team are supporting young talent through their junior programme and backing grassroots sustainable fuel projects
'We just have to unlock it' - Wolff backing 'top driver' Russell to find breakthrough
His Mercedes team remain convinced Russell will rediscover his best form.

Asked what Russell was fighting hardest at the moment, Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff said: "I don't know, because you can see the pace he had towards the end when he was catching Leclerc. He was fastest out on track.
"But after the tyre changes, the pace wasn't there.
"I just don't know where it is and we have to analyse it, because clearly it's in him, it's in the car, and we just have to unlock it."

detailZh: F1修复马德里赛道、迎接明年西班牙大奖赛的五种方法
马德里赛道的首次F1亮相或许在赛场之外取得了成功，但比赛中缺乏精彩对抗，招致了大量批评，也为明年的西班牙大奖赛留下了许多反馈
备受期待的F1重返马德里因比赛缺乏精彩对抗而让车迷们感到意犹未尽，不过马德里赛道本身举办了一场相当体面的赛事。以下是主办方在第二年改进这项赛事的五种方法
总体而言，作为一场首次举办的赛事，马德里45年来的首场F1比赛进行得相当顺利。主办方计划充分利用IFEMA会展中心现有的设施，以及其便捷的公共交通和巴拉哈斯国际机场的交通条件
初步迹象表明，这项计划执行得相当不错，在一座城市中心举办的大型观赛活动中，几乎没有出现通常伴随而来的种种糟糕情况。除了要应付少数过于严苛的保安或警察之外，可容纳11万人的观众进出场地都相当顺畅。
但F1首先是一项赛车运动，因此马德里赛道最需要做好的核心项目就是赛道上的比赛产品。而这方面却差强人意。虽然排位赛颇具观赏性，但这条5.4公里长的赛道尽管是从一张白纸全新设计而来，却完全没有提供任何超车机会。
车手们对超车机会的匮乏感到不满。
马德里赛道之所以呈现如今的面貌，有很多原因。围绕展览馆群的南部区域天然受限，因为必须绕行现有的高大展览大厅。北部专门建造的部分虽然是全新设计，但IFEMA主办方考虑到未来的展馆和展览会，只能使用空地的其中一部分。再加上层层叠叠的官僚程序，建造一条城市赛道绝非易事。
但这并不能成为最终交付的这条赛道的借口。正如一位车手在看到设计的早期效果图时所说的那样：“这里根本不可能有超车。”
在赛事主办方和国际汽联着手为未来进行改进之际，以下是针对2027年改进这条赛道的五条建议。
马德里赛道最令人恼火的一点，是它坚持采用合并式弯道入口，车手必须在刹车的同时转向，两种作用力争夺轮胎有限的抓地力。这使得某些弯道非常别扭，也让前车很容易防守。
5号弯是最严重的问题，因为从图纸上来看，它是唯一一处能够真正自然发生超车的地方——它紧跟在第一个弯道组合之后最长的一段全油门直路之后。
但除了车辆并线入弯外，这个弯道宽度不足、路肩很高、紧贴护栏，这意味着想要超车几乎没有现实的可能，除非冒着被挤上护栏或被迫驶入沥青缓冲区的风险。
除了摩纳哥之外，大多数其他街道赛道至少都有一个超车机会。马德里赛道的弯道设计扼杀了这一点，据了解，根据车手和国际汽联的反馈，5号弯是2027年将进行重大改造的弯道之一。
狭窄而别扭的减速弯让超车几乎不可能。
营销宣传理所当然地聚焦于“纪念碑弯”，也就是12号弯那宏伟的倾斜弯道，它在F1赛历上是独一无二的。它在电视上看起来还不错，但远远没有体现出它的震撼。自由练习时站在环形弯的内侧，是赛历上最好的现场观赛体验之一，因为这个弯道拥有众多的横坡、半径和高度变化，使它有别于椭圆形赛道那种单一的倾斜弯道。
不过，主办方认为赛车在那里可以走不同线路的想法相当乐观，这个弯本身对比赛产品也没有增加多少价值。紧随其后的一段蛇形路段更是雪上加霜。13号弯是另一个90度的中速弯，护栏位置很别扭，导致完全无法超车。16号弯又是一个组合入口，而在最后几个通往终点大直道的弯角里，赛车只能排成纵队通过。
兰多·诺里斯建议绕过18号和19号弯，打造第二条长直道，然后在20号弯接一个发夹弯，并加宽弯道设计以允许不同的走线，或许还可以增加一些倾角。这还需要重新调整出口处的护栏，因为它们令人恼火地侵占了赛车线。
IFEMA作为场地的一大优势同时也是某种弱点。这个地方太庞大了。这让车队更方便运入和运出物资，给了他们充足的工作空间，甚至未来几年还可以增加其他活动——这些活动在其他地方根本不会有足够的空间。
但在场地内走动非常麻烦，尤其对像迈凯伦这样位于维修区尽头、工程区和接待区之间距离巨大的车队来说更是如此。这让公关团队整个周末都变成了高尔夫球车司机，但并非人人都有车接送。希望这个场地的巨大面积不只是被用来塞进更多贵宾和名人——周日的情形已经给人这种感觉了。
IFEMA场地过于庞大在赛道上也带来了后果。540米长的维修区通道不仅特别长，而且由于既有建筑的限制，中间还设有一段100米的分隔。
由于这场比赛演变成了一场相对简单的一停战术，如此漫长的维修区通道只会进一步打消车队尝试其他策略的念头。当超车几乎不可能时，策略上的差异是唯一能引发超车或为比赛增添看点的方式——除非寄希望于红旗和安全车。
尽管马德里展馆区域是一个极具特色的地标，但赛道其余部分却让人感觉可以位于世界上任何地方。
前车手、如今的评论员兼赛道设计师亚历山大·伍尔兹的说明最为到位。“当我看着这些混凝土通道时，有时候我甚至不知道自己身处哪条街道赛道，”伍尔兹对奥地利广播电台（ORF）说。“我是在澳大利亚，是在瓦伦西亚，还是在马德里？我到底在哪里？
“它们看起来总是千篇一律。这意味着我没能在这么酷的场合代表我的主办城市。其实有很多可以发挥的空间。”
虽然令人心跳加速的拉蒙特门塔尔大弯道是一次成功的加入，但马德里赛道的许多区域看起来毫无特色。
放大视角的转播镜头让马德里赛道的情况雪上加霜，而且要让围绕混凝土展览馆的 比赛（比赛）看起来有吸引力本来就很困难。但一定有办法让人们感觉身处于马德里。否则，这一切的意义何在？
还需要更加用心地改善观众的视线，因为我们收到了大量车迷的投诉：由于混凝土护栏的摆放位置，他们坐在昂贵的大看台座位上却被挡住看不到赛车。这个问题对于明年来说相对容易解决，但遗憾的是起初没能避免。
对马德里赛道来说，最重要的事情是体面地度过第一年。组织方在时间安排上面临很大压力，因此重点放在做好充分准备、为观众提供顺畅且安全的体验上。随着首秀顺利完成，马德里赛道可以开始思考如何整体提升车迷体验。
一些车迷区和普通入场区域看起来空荡荡的，细节也比较粗糙。设计方仿照了蒙扎那种俯瞰主直道的大型颁奖台，但没有能力或信心允许车迷像典型的意大利大奖赛那样冲进赛道、真正参与到庆祝之中。正如其他分站发生的意外所表明的，冲进赛道并不容易保障安全，所以第一年组织方保持谨慎是可以理解的。
只有少数车迷能够参与颁奖台庆祝活动，因为组织方在第一年选择了稳妥行事。
无论是在赛道上还是赛道外，马德里赛道都有很多机会提升自己的水准，而为期10年的合同也给了它足够的喘息空间，让它有望成为赛历上深受喜爱的组成部分。
“这只是第一步，”赛事常务董事路易斯·加西亚·阿巴德在比赛结束后接受Motorsport.com采访时说道。“我们在观众和接待方面取得了巨大成功，现在我们对未来几年有很多想法。”
“我们有空间，有场地，有设施，也有能力做到这一点。我相信一级方程式管理公司、国际汽联和我们自己都会去努力。如果有什么可以改进的地方，我们就会去做。”
detailEn: Five ways F1 can fix the Madring for next year's Spanish GP
The Madring's Formula 1 debut may have been an off-track success, but its lack of action has triggered plenty of criticism and feedback for next year's Spanish Grand Prix

F1's much-anticipated return to Madrid has left fans of the series wanting due to a lack of action, though the Madring venue itself put on a respectable event. Here are five ways organisers could improve the event for year two.

By and large, Madrid's first F1 race in 45 years ran particularly smooth for a first-time event. The organisers planned to capitalise on the IFEMA fairgrounds' existing facilities and their easy access to public transportation and to the Barajas International Airport.

Early indications are that that plan worked rather well, with few if any of the typical horror stories accompanying a mass spectator event in the middle of a city. Other than dealing with a few overzealous security guards or police officers, the 110,000 capacity crowd was able to get in and out of the venue rather smoothly.

But F1 is a motor race first and foremost, so the biggest ticket item the Madring needed to get right was its on-track product. It left a lot to be desired. While qualifying was an enticing spectacle, the 5.4km circuit offered zero overtaking opportunities despite being drawn up from a blank sheet of paper.
Drivers were left unimpressed with the lack of overtaking opportunities.

There are plenty of reasons why the Madring circuit is the way it is. The southern part around the complex is inherently limited because of the existing, towering exhibition halls which need navigating around. The northern, purpose-built part was a blank sheet design, but IFEMA organisers could only use a part of the empty plot of land of the track with future pavilions and expositions in mind. Add in the layers of bureaucracy involved, and building an urban race circuit is no easy feat.
But that's no excuse for the circuit that was eventually delivered. As one racing driver put it when he saw an early mock-up of the design: "There's not going to be any overtaking here."
As organisers and the FIA work on improvements for the future, here are five suggestions to improve the venue for 2027.

The most annoying aspect of the Madring was its insistence on drawing combined corner entries, where drivers have to brake and steer at the same time, both forces competing for a limited amount of tyre grip. It made certain corners very awkward and also made it easy for the car in front to defend.
Turn 5 is the worst offender, because on paper it was the only spot where overtaking could actually happen organically, following the longest flat/out section coming out of the first corner sequence.

But alongside the combined entry, the corner's lack of width, presence of high kerbs and proximity of the walls meant there was no realistic way to pass without risking being put into the wall or forced through the asphalt runoff area.

Other than Monaco, most other street circuits feature at least one passing opportunity. Madrid's corner design thwarted that, and it is understood Turn 5 is one of the corner that will undergo significant changes for 2027 following feedback by the drivers and the FIA.
Narrow, awkward chicanes made overtaking all but impossible.

Marketing efforts understandably focused on La Monumental, the majestic banking in Turn 12 which is unique on the F1 calendar. It looked okay on TV, but that didn't nearly do it justice. Standing on the inside of the loop in free practice was one of the better trackside thrills on the calendar because of the corner's many camber, radius and elevation changes that set it apart from an oval-style baking.

Organisers were rather optimistic to think that cars could take different lines through there, though, and the corner didn't add much value to the racing product itself. Its cause wasn't helped by the snaking section that followed. Turn 13 was another 90-degree medium-speed corner with awkward barrier placement that didn't allow for any passing. Turn 16 had another combined entry, while it was single-file through the final few corners towards the finish straight.

Lando Norris suggested a bypass of Turns 18 and 19 to create a second long straight followed by a hairpin in Turn 20, widening its design to allow different approaches, perhaps adding some camber, too. That would also involve realigning the exit barriers, as they annoyingly encroached on the racing line.

One of IFEMA's biggest advantages as a venue was also somewhat of a weakness. The place is enormous. That made it easier for teams to ship freight in and out and gave them plenty of space to work, and perhaps even add other activities in following years that they would never have the space for elsewhere.

But getting around was cumbersome, especially for a team like McLaren which was at the far end of the pitlane, creating a massive distance between its engineering hubs and hospitality units. It turned PR teams into golf car drivers for the weekend, but not everyone was as lucky to be ferried around. Hopefully the ground's massive size isn't just used to cram even more VIPs and celebrities into the venue, which already felt the case on Sunday.
There's also an on-track consequence to IFEMA's vast size. The 540-metre pitlane was not only particularly long, but also featured a 100-metre split in the middle dictated by existing buildings.

With the race turning into a relatively straightforward one-stopper, having such a long pitlane only further discouraged teams from attempting alternative strategies. When overtaking is almost impossible, strategic variance is the only way to induce it or otherwise spice up the race - short of hoping for red flags and safety cars.
As much as La Monumental was a distinctive landmark, the rest of the circuit felt like it could have been anywhere in the world.

Former driver and now pundit and track designer Alex Wurz explained it best. "When I look at this concrete channel, at some point I wouldn't know which street circuit I'm on anymore," Wurz told ORF. "Am I in Australia, am I in Valencia, am I in Madrid, where am I?
"They all always look the same. That means I'm not representing my host city in such a cool way. There's quite a lot you could do there."
While the hair-raising La Monumental banking was a successful addition, many areas of the Madring circuit looked nondescript.

The Madring's case wasn't helped by the zoomed-in viewing angles and it was always going to be tricky to make racing around concrete exhibition halls look attractive. But there has to be a way to make people feel they are in Madrid. Otherwise, what is the point?

More care also needs to be taken to improve sightlines for spectators, as we received plenty of complaints from fans being blocked from seeing the cars from their expensive grandstand seats because of the concrete barrier placement. That's an issue that's relatively straightforward to resolve for next year, but it's a shame it couldn't have been prevented to begin with.

For Madrid, the most important thing was to get through year one respectably. The organisers were up against it in terms of timelines, so the focus was on being ready to provide a smooth and safe experience. With its debut out of the way, the Madring can start thinking about elevating the fan experience in general.

Some fan zones and general admission areas looked sparse and rough around the edges. Designers copied Monza's sprawling podium overlooking the main straight, but weren't able or confident to allow for a typical Italian GP style track invasion for fans to actually be part of the celebration. As shown by incidents at other races, a track invasion is not easy to pull off, so it's understandable why organisers have been prudent in year one.
Only few fans were able to take part in the podium celebrations as organisers played it safe in year one.

Both on and off the track, there are plenty of opportunities for the Madring to step up its game, and its 10-year contract is giving it the breathing room to do so and become a beloved part of the calendar.

"This is the first step," the race's managing director Luis Garcia Abad told Motorsport.com after the race. "We had a big success in terms of public and hospitality, and now we have a lot of ideas for the next few years.
"We have the space, we have a venue, we have the facilities, we have the capacity to do it. I'm sure that FOM, FIA, and ourselves, we will try. If we can improve something, we will do it."

detailZh: 梅赛德斯解释乔治·拉塞尔在马德里为何在VSC下进站

梅赛德斯副领队布拉德利·洛德解释了乔治·拉塞尔在F1西班牙大奖赛中为何在虚拟安全车下进站，尽管他是以硬胎起步。
拉塞尔是顶级车队中唯一没有在马德里这条超车极其困难的赛道上坚持一停策略的车手，这主要与VSC介入的时机有关。

然而，查尔斯·勒克莱尔和拉塞尔等人以硬胎起步。勒克莱尔留在赛道上并领跑至第45圈进站，而梅赛德斯车手在VSC下换上了中性胎，然后在第28圈换回硬胎。
与此同时，梅赛德斯队友兼积分榜领先者基米·安东内利在VSC时机有利、杆位得主诺里斯被排除后获胜。
“VSC对乔治的作用非常不同，它出现在对他最糟糕的时刻，因为他以硬胎起步，本打算跑长距离并利用比赛后期的任何事件，”洛德详细说道。
“他以第6位硬胎起步进入比赛，计划一停。当VSC出动时，他是硬胎中仅次于勒克莱尔法拉利的第二辆车。因此我们叫乔治‘与勒克莱尔相反地进站’。
“为什么？因为如果我们不这样做，他就会简单地跟随勒克莱尔到终点。提前进站的机会非常非常有限，而对于轮胎年龄相近的赛车来说，超车的机会几乎不存在。
“所以我们让乔治换上了中性胎。我们知道中性胎无法跑完剩余的43圈，但通过做一些不同的事情——乔治跑了20圈，然后我们换回硬胎，因为你希望尽可能多地在比赛中使用硬胎。
“乔治随后展现了非常令人印象深刻的表现。他足够快，实际上把勒克莱尔拖进了维修区，可能比法拉利希望的要早，这样把勒克莱尔拖了进来，给了基米前方的干净空气，但随后乔治在最后几圈用相当脆弱的软胎向勒克莱尔施压，最终以仅落后0.7秒完赛。
“赛后乔治非常务实，他说他并不认为我们做什么会有区别，无论是让他留在外面还是进站，鉴于在马德里超车的难度，他很可能总是以第5名完赛。”
尽管以0.4秒的优势做出最快圈速，拉塞尔的低排名结果再次打击了他的冠军希望。这位英国人现在落后安东内利81分，并公开表示他“极不可能”甚至争夺冠军。
detailEn: Mercedes explains why George Russell pitted under VSC at Madring
The timing of the VSC was highly detrimental to Russell’s race in Madrid, and it was perhaps surprising for him to pit then; Mercedes has expanded on its strategy call
Mercedes deputy team principal Bradley Lord has explained why George Russell pitted under the virtual safety car despite starting on hard tyres in Formula 1’s Spanish Grand Prix.
Russell was the only driver from the top teams not to stick to a one-stop on a Madring track where overtaking was at a premium, which was largely down to the timing of the VSC intervention.

Race control neutralised the race at the end of lap 14, which played into the hands of the top four drivers, who started on medium or soft tyres – except Lando Norris, who was already past the pitlane entry when the VSC was announced.

The likes of Charles Leclerc and Russell, however, started the race on the hard compound. Leclerc stayed out and led the race until his lap-45 pitstop, while the Mercedes driver switched to mediums under the VSC and then back to hards on lap 28.
Meanwhile, Mercedes team-mate and championship leader Kimi Antonelli triumphed after the fortunate timing of the neutralisation took polesitter Norris out of his way.

“The VSC worked very differently for George, it fell at the worst possible time for him given that he'd started the race on hards and was looking to run long and capitalise on any events later in the race,” Lord detailed.

“He headed into the race starting on the hard tyre from P6 with a plan to do a one-stop. When the VSC came out he was the second car running on the hard tyre behind Leclerc's Ferrari. Therefore we called for George to do a ‘box opposite to Leclerc’.

“Why? Because had we not done so he would have simply followed Leclerc to the finish. The opportunity to undercut was very, very limited, and the opportunity to overtake was almost non-existent for cars on similar age tyres.

“So we put George onto the medium. We knew that medium wasn't going to be able to do 43 laps to the end, but in doing something different – so George did a 20-lap stint, and then we jumped back onto the hard tyre, because you wanted to be on that hard tyre for as much of the race as possible.

“George then unleashed some really impressive performance. He was going quick enough that he actually pulled Leclerc into the pits probably earlier than Ferrari had wanted to and so that pulled Leclerc in, gave Kimi the free air up front but also then George was pressuring Leclerc in those final laps on that soft tyre that was quite fragile, and actually ended the race only 0.7 seconds behind.

“After the race George was very pragmatic, he said he didn't really think it mattered what we'd have done, whether we'd have left him out or boxed him, he was always likely to finish in P5 given the difficulty of overtaking at the Madring.”

Despite setting the fastest lap by four tenths, Russell’s lowly result was another blow to his championship hopes. The Briton now lies 81 points adrift of Antonelli and openly feels “exceptionally unlikely” to even fight for the title.

items.summaryEn: The Race Of Champions has announced the first four drivers for its inaugural New Zealand event, led by four-time Formula 1 world champion Sebastian Vettel, taking place at Wellington's Hnry Stadium on 9-10 January 2027.
detailZh: F1世界冠军领衔车王争霸赛新西兰首站车手阵容
2027年车王争霸赛公布首批四位车手
车王争霸赛公布了其新西兰首站的首批四位车手，该赛事将于2027年1月9日至10日在惠灵顿的Hnry Stadium举行。
阵容由四届F1世界冠军塞巴斯蒂安·维特尔领衔，自2007年以来他仅缺席过两届车王争霸赛。这位德国车手曾与迈克尔·舒马赫搭档，在2007年至2012年连续六年赢得国家杯，并于2017年与帕斯卡尔·维尔莱茵搭档再次夺冠；他还在2015年伦敦的正赛中获胜。
“在悉尼车王争霸赛之前，我第一次快速访问了新西兰，被这个国家的美丽所震撼，所以我开玩笑地对组织者说，‘你们能不能把下一届车王争霸赛带到新西兰来？’”维特尔说。“我真的很期待在一月份于惠灵顿举行的车王争霸赛中与来自全球的众多其他冠军同场竞技，并有机会游览更多新西兰的地方。”
一位现役F1车手也已公布，那就是瓦尔特利·博塔斯；这位十次大奖赛冠军得主，目前效力于垫底的凯迪拉克车队，将第三次参加该赛事。
海登·帕顿，现代世界拉力车队的现代i20 N Rally1赛车
其他系列赛也将有代表参加，包括2025年Supercars冠军查兹·莫斯特，他在去年于澳大利亚举行的上一届车王争霸赛中完成了首秀，以及新西兰明星海登·帕顿，他曾一次赢得WRC分站冠军。
“看到世界上最具观赏性的赛车运动赛事之一首次来到新西兰，真是太棒了，”帕顿说。“新西兰目前在许多领域都处于赛车运动的黄金时代，我想不出比举办车王争霸赛更合适的庆祝方式了，它吸引了来自世界各地的众多大牌明星。
“对于新西兰赛车迷来说，这真是一个千载难逢的机会，可以近距离接触来自F1、WRC、场地赛和其他赛车形式的车手，他们将在新西兰最著名的体育场馆之一内驾驶同等赛车展开较量。由于诸多原因，这确实是一场历史性的赛事，我个人非常自豪能参与其中。”
detailEn: F1 world champion among drivers for Race Of Champions’ first New Zealand event
The first four drivers for the 2027 ROC have been announced
The Race Of Champions has announced the first four drivers for its inaugural New Zealand event, taking place at Wellington’s Hnry Stadium on 9-10 January 2027.

The lineup will be spearheaded by four-time Formula 1 world champion Sebastian Vettel, who has taken part in all but two Race Of Champions events since 2007. The German won the Nations’ Cup six years in a row, from 2007 to 2012, alongside Michael Schumacher, and in 2017 with Pascal Wehrlein; he also triumphed in the main contest in London in 2015.

“Before ROC Sydney I went for a first quick visit to New Zealand and was blown away by the beauty of the country, so I told the organisers jokingly, ‘Can you please bring the next ROC to New Zealand?’,” Vettel said. “I am really looking forward to competing against so many other champions from across the globe at the Race Of Champions in Wellington in January, and getting a chance to visit more of New Zealand.”
A current F1 driver has also been announced in Valtteri Bottas; the 10-time grand prix winner, now racing for backmarker Cadillac, will take part in the event for just the third time.
Hayden Paddon, Hyundai World Rally Team Hyundai i20 N Rally1

Other series will also be represented with 2025 Supercars champion Chaz Mostert, who made his Race Of Champions debut last time out that same year in Australia, and New Zealand star Hayden Paddon, a one-time WRC rally winner.

“It’s amazing to see one of the world’s most spectacular motorsport events come to New Zealand for the first time ever,” Paddon said. “New Zealand is really in a golden age of motorsport at the moment across so many disciplines, and I can’t think of a more fitting celebration of this than hosting the Race Of Champions, that attracts so many of the biggest stars from all around the world.

“This is really a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity for Kiwi motorsport fans to get up close and personal with drivers from F1, WRC, circuit and other motorsport forms, all battling it out in equal machinery inside one of New Zealand’s most famous sports stadiums. It’s really a historic event for so many reasons, and I’m personally incredibly proud to be a part of it.”
